text: Email, post, mail. So you write a letter, right? The transmitter is like sending letters, and each letter, of course, is made of several symbols. And then it sends the letter through the postal mail toward a destination. At least in the old times, we used that. Now we have emails, but the concept is the same. You write an email. It is intended for your friend. Your friend is the destination. You are the transmitter, and what you send is an email, a message, right? You don't send one letter, A, B, C at a time. You send the message. That's the same idea. In in internet, we transmit packets, and a packet is a chunk of bits. Now, when you send an email or a postal letter to your friend, what you do is not just send the sheet of paper with the information, right, that you want to send to your friend, but you write your name, your address, the name and the address of of your friend. Otherwise, you will never reach your friend. Same for the packets. The packets need an header, and in this header, at minimum, you have to write who is the sender of the packet and who is the destination of the packet.
